items.item_text: Oversees the Office of K-20 Regional Alliances and reports to the Associate Vice Chancellor of Educational Partnerships. Acts on the vision and strategies of the region to increase capacity, strengthen leadership, increase capacity, and develop partnerships with K-12, postsecondary, and workforce. Provides research that helps evaluate and inform procedural systems for K-12 preparation program administration. Incumbent displays advanced expertise in identifying research-based innovative approaches to K-20 student, parent, and district- centered services that enable the Center for Educational Partnerships to demonstrate high levels of success in working with K-12, postsecondary, and workforce.

Demonstrates experience in improving educational and economic outcomes for young people through a systems approach. Daily oversight of the Office of K-20 Regional Alliances. Addresses inquiries from the Center for Educational Partnerships Associate Vice Chancellor, WE Will! Collaborative, campus, and/or sponsor agencies regarding K-20 program administration. Oversees and conducts ongoing review/evaluation of office, collaboratives’ outcomes, and systemic impact. Ability to act in context with the distinct landscape and culture of each of the regions that UC Merced serves.

Evaluates the effectiveness of the Office of K-20 Regional Alliances and the WE Will! Collaborative’s service to a broad range of audiences, including the state legislature, University of California Office of the President, campus administration, K-12 school districts, postsecondary, and workforce. In partnership with the Center for Educational Partnerships’ (CEP) Data Analysis and Evaluation reviews outcomes and relevant research and makes recommendations to support the WE Will! Collaborative! and enhance CEP’s programming. Participate in developing and monitoring policies and procedures for CEP’s data collection and tool enhancements for unit efficiency. Assists Associate Vice Chancellor in developing measurable ways to assess the effectiveness of academic preparation programs and districtwide partnerships.

As part of the Center for Educational Partnerships (CEP) leadership team, supports the Associate Vice Chancellor of Educational Partnerships and collaborates with the Directors of the Offices of K-14 Federal Projects and State Academic Preparation and Educational Partnerships (SAPEP) in the development of strategic program plans, setting targets, systemic interventions, and policies and procedures. Monitors the progress of the WE Will! Collaborative and K-20 regional alliances and supports their established objectives. Oversees the development, enhancement, and tracking of databases, dashboards, indicators, and tools. Oversees data compilation for grant submissions, monitoring, and reporting.

Demonstrates risk taking and the ability to have courageous conversations to navigate the WE Will! and K-20 regional collaboratives’ distinctive features of particular situations or activity. Understand the importance of data informed decisions and model that in all decisions and approaches. General oversight in the implementation of K-12 trainings for administrators, faculty, staff, and students on K-12 research, state accountability frameworks, policies, and procedures. Works with CEP administrators to facilitate all ancillary processes involved in developing a grant proposals, pre-awards, and the data analysis and evaluation research projects.

Understands budget development, monitoring and revisions for high quality and accurate reporting to the Associate Vice Chancellor, campus, WE Will! Collaborative, K-12, postsecondary, and workforce partners and funders. Understand the importance of marketing and messaging the vision and goals of the region regularly and often. Ability to engage and sustain key partners from K12, postsecondary and workforce.

Leads the operation and facilitation of the WE Will! Collaborative and the development of plans and professional learning sessions to coach K-12 district staff on using data to identify gaps and pursue evidence-based interventions to close equity and access gaps. Identifies and advices on improvement strategies that aim to close the achievement gap. Promotes policies and services that provide multiple levels of support for K-20 educational partnership efforts, such as technical training and workshops related to academic standards, strategies to increase college eligibility, pathways, admission/ enrollment trends, and workforce. Demonstrates competencies as a facilitators, communicator, and connector.

Demonstrates extensive experience in intersegmental, multi-sector systems with proven outcomes for the system and the students it serves. Uses data dashboards and data tools to inform and improve educational practices. Identifies systemic gaps and presents them to stakeholders to inform change. In partnership with the Office of Data Analysis and Evaluation and Technical Assistance (DAE-TA), generates summary reports of findings and shares with stakeholders. Works closely with DAE-TA to perform ongoing evaluation of outcomes and interventions. Reviews outcomes and relevant research and makes recommendations for ways to utilize research to support and enhance the work of the Center for Educational Partnerships to adopt evidence-based practices to improve student outcomes.
